Alex — thanks for the heads up and for sending the MAP_v2. I skimmed the change and this looks like the classic procurement-driven slip (we've seen this pattern several times). A few quick notes / asks: 

- Two-week canary: we can stand up a targeted canary for the 25% traffic slice on the dedicated pool without reconfiguring model mounts. Grace can confirm infra capacity; on first pass it seems OK but I want to confirm autoscaling headroom.
- SLA/credits: we don't automatically give credits for procurement-caused acceptance delays. That said, I can route a one-time temporary SLA concession + standby escrow option to leadership for approval if it materially helps the deal close on the revised window.
- Acceptance criteria: please confirm whether HelioHealth still plans to run the full eval suite (latency P95, throughput baseline, custom prompt regressions) during the canary or if it's a smoke-only engagement. That will change how aggressively we size and whether we keep prefix caching warm.

Grace / Marissa — can you weigh in on capacity and whether we should propose the standby-escrow language (documented in the attached SLA-exception-request.pdf) to their legal? If yes, I will escalate to get sign-off for a single exception and a small credit tied to acceptance lag.

Alex — once we align, I propose a brief sync tomorrow to confirm the exact canary start date and acceptance checklist.

Best,
Aditya
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Aditya / Marissa —

Capacity check: we have a node buffer in the HelioHealth dedicated pool that will support a 2-week canary at 25% traffic with current quantization/instance profile. Operational plan below (proposal for MAP_v2 execution):

- Day 0 (canary start): route 25% production traffic to canary nodes, preserve prefix cache for the top-10 prompt families, enable detailed tracing for the canary route.
- Day 1-3: run full eval suite nightly (latency P50/P95/P99, regression checks on 120 prompt set, token-usage delta). We fail the canary if any regression > 6% or P95 increases > 30ms vs baseline.
- Day 4-10: expand to 60% if metrics stable for 48 hours; continue nightly evaluations.
- Acceptance window: if HelioHealth confirms acceptance criteria (as listed in MAP_v2) we will consider final sign-off after 48 hours at 100% with no critical regressions.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Procurement review could introduce contract redlines that require a DocuSign addendum; mitigation: standby-escrow clause and a 1x goodwill credit (0.5% of monthly forecast) to be approved by leadership.
- Data residency ask: if they re-request VPC routing changes that require infra rework, that could re-open the window. We need their legal to sign the scope.

Ask: Aditya / Marissa, I recommend we offer the standby-escrow + 1x credit as a one-time concession and attach a strict acceptance checklist and expiration date (two weeks). If leadership greenlights, I can own the canary execution and daily health notes that we'll share with HelioHealth procurement/legal.
